reason: Alderwick's quote (event-013, move-out-works-quotation.pdf, ref NBL-027-Q1) is for the right property, 46 Fernwick Lane, from the assigned provider, and totals £3,865.68. That is far above the £300 approval limit. The workflow note (event-002) said approval is "normally" in place, but no landlord approval appears anywhere in the case, so I treated none as given. Maya has already asked Owen Vale to approve the quote (event-014, 13:53 on 15 Sep) and has noted she is waiting (event-016). The follow-up call (event-017) captured only a recording notice and an unclear utterance, so it is not an approval or a rejection. The landlord's reply is not overdue, because chasing is allowed after 3 days and only about 2.5 hours have passed. ROUTE_FOR_APPROVAL would only repeat the request already sent, and Alderwick must not be instructed without written approval. Nothing is unsafe: the property is vacant and no hazard is reported, so P3 applies. The checkout report does mention a taped boiler casing needing inspection, a non-working smoke detector and reported water ingress, so these should be dealt with before re-letting. The quote has a single lump sum with no itemisation and no exclusions. It leaves out the kitchen worktop, flooring, carpets, boiler inspection, curtains and bulbs. It also lacks an attendance date and says nothing on VAT. The landlord should know this when deciding. The reference mismatch flagged between the report and the quote is only two different document types, not a real conflict. I scheduled a follow-up for 72 hours. A decision would change if the landlord approves in writing (instruct Alderwick), rejects or queries the quote, or stays silent past 3 days (chase, then a call or escalation).
